texts.preamble: Firojkhan Mehmudkha Pathan vs State Of Maharashtra on 14 July, 2020
texts.facts: 2. The applicant is seeking bail in the event of his arrest in connection with Crime/FIR No.335/2020 registered with Bhokardan Police Station, District Jalna for the offences punishable under Sections 328, 188, 272, 273 of the Indian Penal Code and Sections 26, 26(2)(iv), 27(2)(e) and 59 of Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006. 2 ABA503-2020 3. In sum and substance, the allegations are to the effect that huge stock of scented tobacco/gutkha was found being transported in a vehicle. On enquiry with the driver, he had disclosed about having purchased the stock from Firojkhan Mahemudkhan i.e. the applicant. The goods were seized. The FIR was lodged by a police officer effecting the raid and the crime was registered. Firojkhan Mehmudkha Pathan vs State Of Maharashtra on 14 July, 2020 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/24305200/ 1 4.
texts.arguments: The learned Advocate for the applicant submits that the applicant is being sought to be implicated merely on the basis of a statement of a co-accused, which is not admissible in evidence. Except the offence punishable under Section 328 of the IPC, the rest of the offences being invoked are bailable. There are no allegations about applicant having administered any poisonous substance to anybody, which is a necessary ingredient for constituting the offence punishable under Section 328 of the IPC. In a matter before a Division Bench of this Court as well as in the matters before the Single Judges of this Court, it has been consistently held that administration of poisonous substance is a necessary ingredient for constituting the offence punishable under Section 328 of the IPC and that being absent, the applicant be granted anticipatory bail. The applicant is ready to cooperate the Investigating Officer. She submits that the offence is serious.
